conservation.condition_narrative: The drawing is unfixed, complete, and retains all the original structural and material elements applied by the artist at the time of fabrication. The mounting is secure, and the mat and backing materials are stable. There are handling finger dents that are best seen in raking illumination, at either side and below the mid-point of the vertical dimension. There are repetitive cockles across the top and bottom edges, possibly as a result of the historic rolling of the sheet. There are numerous inclusions in the paper.
conservation.technical_description:
**Support:** The support is a sheet of medium-thick, cream-colored, slightly textured, Ingres-type laid paper. Chain lines move vertically across the composition. There is a watermark in the lower viewer's right corner in reverse that reads "MICHALLET (France)." 
 
 
 
**Ground or Support Preparation:** There is no visible sizing or fixative visible in normal or UV light, although dilute gelatin sizing would be difficult to see, even in UV. 
 
 
 
**Design Layers:** Charcoal is applied with dense, curvelinear outlining and with various degrees of shading, fill, and overlap. There is no subtractive work visible. 
 
 
 
**Surface Coating:** No fixative or surface coating is visible. 
 
 
 
**Framing, Backing, and Hanging Hardware:** The work is framed in a 2006 white wash maple frame with secondary basswood backing and strainer. The over-matted 8-ply, cotton-finer Rising Museum mounting board (warm-white) window mat is folio taped to the 4-ply backing mat of the same type. The sandwich system of Optium tin-titanium optically coated acrylic is sealed to an acid-free, zeolite- and charcoal-embedded backing board. An insulating panel of acid-free Fome-Cor board is added to the back.

description: This work illustrates the industrial landscape surrounding the East River.  The river, on which a boat is visible, bisects the scene horizontally.  In the foreground, several buildings line the various streets that lead to the river bank.  On the opposite side of the river, smokestacks rise above factories. This artwork has *Untitled (New York)*, 1932 (cat. no. 803) on the back.
